description: Run a raw, read-only SPARQL SELECT against the CELLAR Virtuoso endpoint — an escape hatch for CDM ontology traversals the curated tools do not cover. Only SELECT is accepted; update forms and ASK/CONSTRUCT/DESCRIBE are rejected before execution, and results are capped at the server row cap (100 by default). The cdm:, skos:, and xsd: prefixes are auto-injected.

sparql_query.description: A read-only SPARQL SELECT query. Leading comments and PREFIX/BASE declarations are allowed; the cdm:, skos:, and xsd: prefixes are auto-injected. LIMIT is injected at the server row cap (100 unless the deployment configures a lower one) if absent, or capped to it; to read past the cap, add ORDER BY and repeat the query with OFFSET raised by the cap (a sorted query reaches row 10,000 at most). Key CDM predicates: cdm:resource_legal_id_celex (CELEX), cdm:work_date_document (date), cdm:work_has_resource-type (type), cdm:work_is_about_concept_eurovoc (EuroVoc subject), cdm:work_cites_work (citation). CELEX is an xsd:string literal — match it as a typed triple, ?work cdm:resource_legal_id_celex "32016R0679"^^xsd:string (an untyped literal matches nothing, in a triple or in FILTER(?celex = "…"), and a FILTER(STR(…)) comparison scans every CELEX). For text, use bif:contains with a single-quoted phrase.

timeout_hint.description: Optional client-side timeout in milliseconds (1000–55000). The server default (55000 unless the deployment configures another value) applies when omitted.

name: eurlex_query_sparql

bindings.description: Raw SPARQL binding rows. To extract a value from a row: row["varName"]?.value. Use the variables array to iterate in query order.

items.description: A single SPARQL result row. Each key is a SELECT variable name; each value is a SPARQL term object with "type" ("uri", "literal", or "bnode") and "value" (the string value), plus "datatype" (an IRI) on a typed literal or "xml:lang" (a language tag) on a language-tagged literal — the two are mutually exclusive. A variable left unbound by an OPTIONAL has no key in the row at all.

cap.description: The server-enforced result ceiling that was applied.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `not_read_only`: The query is a SPARQL Update operation (INSERT, DELETE, WITH, LOAD, CLEAR, CREATE, DROP, COPY, MOVE, or ADD). `unsupported_query_form`: The query is not a SELECT: an ASK, CONSTRUCT, or DESCRIBE form, an unrecognized keyword, or no query keyword after the prologue. `sparql_error`: CELLAR rejected the query: a syntax or semantic error, a compile error, or a sorted query whose OFFSET + LIMIT passes row 10,000 (SR353, answered with its own recovery: lower OFFSET or narrow the query). The same query fails the same way again. `sparql_timeout`: The query ran past the client-side timeout (timeout_hint, default 55 s), or Virtuoso refused it as over its estimated-cost limit. Neither is retried: the call fails inside the configured bound. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

notice.description: On a truncated result: how to page past the row cap with ORDER BY and OFFSET, and the 10,000-row limit on a sorted query. On a zero-row result whose query has an untyped string literal as a triple object: how to type or language-tag it, since CELLAR stores identifiers as typed literals that an untyped one never matches.

shown.description: Number of binding rows returned in this response.

total.description: Number of binding rows returned (at most the server's row cap, 100 by default).

truncated.description: True when the server's row cap (the deployment's configured cap, 100 by default; cap gives the value applied) limited the rows and more may exist upstream — page on with ORDER BY in the query and OFFSET raised by the cap per call (sorted queries reach row 10,000 at most), or narrow the query with FILTERs.

variables.description: Variable names from the SELECT head, in query order.

items.description: A SELECT variable name, in the order declared in the query.

title: Raw CELLAR SPARQL Query
